From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Internal, privileged, for the Wattlebridge deal team. Do not send this analysis to the Seller.**

## Preliminary point: the "[STANDARD]" labels

The Seller's cover note asks us to treat items marked [STANDARD] as "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and to focus only on [OPEN] items. We should not accept that approach. Nothing in the file shows Wattlebridge agreed to any of these positions. Most of the [STANDARD] items are direct departures from our playbook. The "FINAL / not to be re-opened" label and the market-context assertions (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 month limitation periods) are the Seller's characterisations, not agreed terms, and our playbook governs. We should review every clause.

We also have no record of written authority from Amelia Frost for any fallback. Several Seller positions sit close to our fallbacks, but none is authorised, so none can be conceded yet.

## Material departures and pushback

### 1. General Warranty cap (Cl. 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4.8m. **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6.0m.
- The Seller's figure matches our conditional fallback, but that fallback requires Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None has been given.
- **Pushback:** Reject and hold at AUD 6.0m. The gap is AUD 1.2m.

### 2. Thresholds (Cl. 12.2)
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; recovery only of the excess above the basket.
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
- This is a significant departure. The Seller's version is a deductible, not a tipping basket.
- **Illustration:** for an AUD 300,000 aggregate claim, our position recovers the full AUD 300,000. The Seller's draft recovers AUD 50,000 (300k minus the 250k deductible). Claims under AUD 25,000 are also excluded entirely under the Seller's draft.
- **Pushback:** Reject both figures and the excess-only mechanism. Restore first-dollar recovery above a AUD 50,000 basket and a AUD 5,000 de minimis.

### 3. Time limits (Cl. 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months for General Warranty Claims, and any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise.
- **Playbook:** 24 months for general claims. 18 months is a fallback requiring Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- The "applies to all Claims" wording is a hidden general-regime override. It would pull Title, Tax, IP and other categories into the general limitation period, which the playbook prohibits.
- **Pushback:** Reject 18 months and restore 24 months. Strike the cross-application language and keep each category's time limit separate.

### 4. Fundamental / Title claims
- **Seller:** capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Playbook:** separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- This is a fundamental departure. Title and capacity risk is the buyer's core exposure in a 100% share acquisition.
- **Pushback:** Reject outright. Restore the separate Fundamental regime as described in the playbook.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (Cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** apply to "all Claims of any nature." No fraud carve-out appears.
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Pushback:** Insert the carve-out, drafted as non-waivable. Without it, the non-reliance clause could bar claims based on the Seller's own fraud.

### 6. Disclosure (DL 1.1, 1.2; Schedule 7)
- **Seller:** general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. DL 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to" in the data room.
- **Playbook:** reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. Require specific fair disclosure.
- The effect of DL 1.1 would be to disclose almost any problem the Buyer could find in the data room, including the matters in DL 2 to 10.
- **Pushback:** Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2 and the Schedule 7 general disclosure. Require specific disclosure against specific warranties.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (Cl. 8.3)
- **Seller:** no Buyer claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must name seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. Never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- The "discoverable" wording converts the Buyer's due diligence into a waiver of claims. This is the most dangerous clause in the package because it would neutralise the disclosed issues below.
- **Pushback:** Delete. If a knowledge qualifier is conceded, limit it to named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, with carve-outs for title, capacity, fraud and specific indemnities.

### 8. Bluefen consent (Cl. 3 / 6.3; DL 2)
- **Seller:** reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." DL 2 confirms no final written consent or evidence of conditions.
- **Playbook:** effective consent plus evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Consent-on-delivery is not acceptable. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (~30%). It is a material customer.
- **Pushback:** Make effective consent, with conditions under cl. 11.3 satisfied, a condition precedent to Completion. Delete the reasonable-endeavours standard and the "satisfied on delivery" language.

### 9. Riverlark facility (Cl. 2 / 7; DL 3)
- **Seller:** approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding, to be addressed by a release "following Completion." DL 3 confirms it has not been repaid and no discharge is included.
- **Playbook:** current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.
- A post-Completion release leaves the Company's assets encumbered with the Buyer funding the debt.
- **Pushback:** Require a current payout letter, direct repayment from the Completion funds flow, and effective releases at Completion. Do not accept a post-Completion release without Frost approval and an irrevocable undertaking.

### 10. Employee bonuses and funds flow (DL 5; funds flow note)
- **Seller:** DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 says on-costs are not addressed.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item in the funds flow or seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Silent exclusion means the Buyer inherits the liability with no funding. On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) are also unquantified.
- **Pushback:** Add a specific funds-flow line for the bonuses, or make them seller-funded, with on-costs quantified and covered. Require a payroll reconciliation.

### 11. Ironquay IP (Cl. 11.1; DL 4)
- **Seller:** the indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate."
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 figure is not independently verified either way.
- DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on payment of every SOW3 fee. Payment of AUD 180,000 alone may not cure a title defect in the materials. DL 4 confirms there is no confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Pushback:** Reject "adequate." Broaden the indemnity to cover failure to transfer SOW3 IP, not only the payment amount. Preserve the cure mechanism. Ask for independent confirmation of the AUD 180,000 balance, without assuming the figure is right or wrong.

### 12. Export / privacy incident (Cl. 4.6 / Sch. 6; DL 6)
- **Seller:** a "preliminary operational matter" that is "not expected to be material."
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- The Seller's materiality view is not supported by its own disclosure, which says scope, access and notification are unknown. Around 1,240 records may include names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps.
- **Pushback:** Do not accept the "not material" characterisation, and do not assert a breach either. Require: preservation of logs, a written investigation scope and timetable, regular written updates, and a warranty on the incident's disclosed facts. My own recommendation, outside the playbook, is to consider a specific indemnity for costs arising from the incident. This should be discussed with Frost before we put it to the Seller.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (DL 8)
- **Seller:** three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Playbook:** assess. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- DL 8 says the disclosure does not state whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. The three renewals of AUD 110,000 each may be one arrangement read together.
- **Pushback:** Request the contracts and the renewal timing. Assess whether they are ordinary-course. Do not accept the characterisation, and do not make an automatic price deduction.

### 14. Tax and IP
- **Seller:** tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime."
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain open. Keep them separate from the general regime.
- **Pushback:** Reject "settled." Confirm these categories remain open and are not subject to the general cap, basket or time limit.

### 15. Title (DL 10; DD-012)
- **Seller:** title to 100% of shares is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Playbook:** DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof. Require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence.
- **Pushback:** Require an ASIC company extract, a PPSR search, an independent check of the share register, an encumbrance search, and evidence of Harbourglass's capacity and authority to sell.

### 16. Other consents and notices (DL 1.4, 7, 9)
- The playbook does not address these directly, but they are relevant. DL 1.4 disclaims that any consent or notice is legally required. Combined with DL 7 (landlord notification, not consent) and DL 9 (Mossvale restriction on assignment), the Seller is avoiding confirmation of whether consents are needed.
- **Pushback:** Require a schedule of all consents, notices and change-of-control provisions, with a specific warranty that the schedule is complete. Confirm with the Seller whether landlord or Mossvale consent is needed.

## Summary of recommendations

| Priority | Item | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | Fundamental/Title regime (4) | Reject. Restore separate 100% cap, six-year period, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar |
| Critical | Fraud carve-out (5) | Insert non-waivable carve-out from all limits |
| Critical | Disclosure (6) and buyer knowledge (7) | Delete whole-data-room disclosure and discoverable-matters exclusion |
| Critical | Bluefen (8) | Effective consent and evidence of conditions as CP to Completion |
| Critical | Riverlark (9) | Payout and release at Completion; no post-completion release without Frost approval |
| High | Funds flow / bonuses (10) | Specific line or seller-funded; quantify on-costs |
| High | Cap, thresholds, time limit (1–3) | Restore 25%/AUD 6m, AUD 5k/50k first-dollar, 24 months; no hidden override |
| High | Ironquay IP (11) | Broaden indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure |
| High | Title (15) | Independent title and encumbrance evidence |
| Medium | Incident (12) | Logs, investigation, updates; consider specific indemnity (needs Frost input) |
| Medium | Sandbar (13) | Assess contracts; no automatic deduction |
| Medium | Tax/IP (14) | Reject "settled"; keep open and separate |
| Medium | Consents (16) | Schedule of consents with completeness warranty |

**Process points:**
- Reject the "[STANDARD]" clearance and "FINAL" labels in writing, and state that Wattlebridge has not agreed to any clause in the package.
- Do not offer the 20% cap, 18-month period or any other fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
- Our response should be a full mark-up, not a selective response to [OPEN] items.

This analysis reflects the playbook and the documents as provided. It is a working review for the deal team, and final drafting and advice should be confirmed with the responsible NSW solicitor before anything goes to the Seller.
